papers.relied_on: Row 50 D8 assumed the study built its diabetes screening algorithm on HbA1c, fasting glucose and OGTT and not on insulin.
papers.full_text_shows: Correct, and the full text adds that fasting insulin and HOMA-IR were tested as single markers and were less accurate than fasting glucose and OGTT. Against the older glucose-based definition AUC was 0.935 (fasting glucose), 0.947 (2-h OGTT), 0.800 (HOMA-IR cut-off 3.38) and 0.722 (fasting insulin cut-off 14.7 mIU/L). The study did not test whether insulin adds to the glucose tests; the reference definition contains fasting glucose and OGTT, so those tests are favoured (incorporation).
papers.quote: In order to best identify newly redefined diabetes, we recommend a simple biochemical algorithm as follows: step 1. HBA1c ≥5.7%
papers.key_numbers: n = 798 on antipsychotics, tested before drug start (diabetes 7.8% old definition, 10.2% new). Old definition: fasting insulin sens 56.5%, spec 81.9%, AUC 0.722; HOMA-IR sens 66.1%, spec 86.7%, AUC 0.800; fasting glucose sens 91.9%, spec 82.5%, AUC 0.935 (cut 98 mg/dL); OGTT 2 h AUC 0.947. New definition: fasting insulin AUC 0.685, HOMA-IR AUC 0.748, HbA1c AUC 0.885, fasting glucose AUC 0.849. Recommended algorithm: HbA1c >=5.7% then conventional tests (85.2% sens, 100% spec by construction).
papers.role_in_work: Adult comparator study for row 50 D8 (added value of fasting insulin over glucose-based alternatives); also gives insulin accuracy data.
papers.design: Single-centre consecutive observational diagnostic-accuracy study, Belgium (Nov 2003 to Jul 2007), cross-sectional with a standardized test battery.
papers.population_and_size: 798 adult psychiatric patients on antipsychotics (first- and second-generation, 41% on treatment >1 year), mean age 37.7, 61% male, 62% smokers, free of diabetes before starting drugs; not children, not limited to second-generation drugs.
papers.measure_type: fasting-based (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR) compared with glucose-based tests (fasting glucose, 75-g OGTT) and HbA1c; no C-peptide.
papers.assay_or_platform: Same laboratory throughout; insulin assay not named in the text read. HOMA-IR from fasting glucose and insulin.
papers.quality_note: Large for the field, but one centre, adult, older era, optimism from data-driven cut points (optimal cut-off chosen on the same data), and incorporation bias for glucose tests. Pre-2010 definition could not be replicated exactly by the authors.

papers.relied_on: Row 27 D7 used '830 TPIAT in 2002 to 2013' from a National Inpatient Sample analysis as a base for the yearly volume.
papers.full_text_shows: The figure is confirmed: 830 TPIAT and 1,705 total pancreatectomies for any pancreatitis, 825 TPIAT for chronic pancreatitis, 2002 to 2013, weighted national estimates from a 20% discharge sample, adults only, neoplasia excluded. It is a 12-year total (about 70 a year on average, rising), not a current annual volume, and the paper contains no C-peptide, insulin or testing data.
papers.quote: is a low volume procedure performed in centers scattered throughout the United States and the world
papers.key_numbers: 1,705 TP and 830 TPIAT (any pancreatitis); 1,006 TP and 825 TPIAT (chronic pancreatitis), 2002 to 2013; TPIAT patients younger (41 vs 50 y) and 69% female; 90% of operations in tertiary academic centres. Year-by-year counts are in figures not in the text read.
papers.role_in_work: Source of the base volume for D7 of row 27 (beta-cell reserve around TPIAT).
papers.design: Retrospective administrative database analysis (HCUP National Inpatient Sample, ICD-9-CM codes).
papers.population_and_size: US adults with total pancreatectomy for pancreatitis with or without islet autotransplant; 830 TPIAT and 1,705 TP (any pancreatitis); excludes neoplasia, age <18 and pregnancy.
papers.measure_type: none (no insulin or C-peptide measure in the paper); used only for patient volume.
papers.quality_note: Coding errors possible; cells under 10 patients excluded; ends in 2013, so the post-2013 trend in the score reason is an extrapolation. Children are excluded, so paediatric TPIAT is not in the count.

papers.relied_on: Row 3 D7 used a hypoglycaemia ED or hospital rate of 5.75 per 1,000 person-years for sulfonylurea-only regimens.
papers.full_text_shows: The rate is in the table as 5.75 (95% CI 5.08 to 6.42) per 1,000 persons per year for sulfonylurea without insulin (49,200 people, 24.4% of the cohort). It counts events with a primary or first diagnosis of hypoglycaemia in a commercially insured and Medicare Advantage claims cohort that had an HbA1c result. Rates are higher with sulfonylurea plus insulin, which the row's chain does not use. The paper does not report whether insulin, C-peptide or a drug screen was sent.
papers.quote: 6.7-fold higher (IRR, 6.73 [95% CI, 4.93-9.22]) among patients treated with sulfonylurea (without insulin)
papers.key_numbers: 201,705 adults with diabetes; overall 9.06 per 1,000 person-years; sulfonylurea alone 5.75; basal insulin 12.39; basal plus bolus insulin plus sulfonylurea 30.87; other medications 0.74; prior event IRR 6.60.
papers.role_in_work: Event-rate input for the D7 chain of row 3 (sulfonylurea hypoglycaemia work-up).
papers.design: Retrospective cohort of claims and laboratory data (OptumLabs Data Warehouse), 2014 to 2016.
papers.population_and_size: 201,705 US adults with diabetes and an HbA1c in 2015, mean age 65.8; insured population only.
papers.measure_type: none (no insulin or C-peptide measure); the paper supplies event rates only.
papers.quality_note: Claims-based, outcome limited to events reaching ED or hospital, not validated by chart review; not nationally representative (insured, with HbA1c). Authors say most severe events are not captured, so the event count is a lower bound.

papers.relied_on: Row 50 D2 and D8 treated this as one small accuracy-type study (n = 55, HOMA-IR cut point 1.98) whose reference standard the abstract did not state, and as showing HOMA-IR rose earlier than single laboratory values.
papers.full_text_shows: The reference standard is HOMA-IR itself: a patient was 'at risk' if the age-, sex- and BMI-specific HOMA-IR percentile was at or above the 75th, and the ROC analysis then looked for the HOMA-IR (and TG/HDL) cut point that predicts that label. The AUC of 0.88 to 0.95 and sensitivity/specificity of 74 to 83% are therefore circular and say nothing about detecting dysglycaemia or outcomes. The 'earlier rise' is a within-group change over a median of 9 months, with no clinical outcome and no comparison of decisions. Text extraction is two-column and partly interleaved; the Methods and Table 4 were readable.
papers.quote: caseness being defined by HOMA-IR percentile
papers.key_numbers: n = 55, mean age 9.9 y, median follow-up 9 months; HOMA-IR AUC 0.88 to 0.95, overall cut point 1.47 (mean) and 1.98 (maximum HOMA-IR), sensitivity and specificity 83%; fasting insulin cut point >25 mU/L from the laboratory (99th percentile); insulin worsened in 75% of children.
papers.role_in_work: Only child-specific study behind the 'marginal' D8 and the 'accuracy-type' wording in D2 of row 50.
papers.design: Prospective single-centre monitoring-protocol implementation study (Tampere, Finland), no control group.
papers.population_and_size: 55 children on second-generation antipsychotics (risperidone 58%, aripiprazole 29%, quetiapine 13% at baseline), mostly boys with developmental and hyperkinetic disorders.
papers.measure_type: fasting-based (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR); no post-load or C-peptide measure.
papers.assay_or_platform: Hospital laboratory (TAUH) insulin; HOMA-IR = glucose (mmol/L) x insulin (mU/L) / 22.5; percentile curves from a published reference.
papers.quality_note: Small, uncontrolled, concurrent psychotropics and haemolysis noted by authors as confounders; circular reference standard. Authors disclose no conflict for two authors; the remaining disclosure text was not fully readable.

papers.relied_on: No score entry cites it; V16 lists it as fetched at abstract level and corpus.csv lists it as V16 text.
papers.full_text_shows: A narrative laboratory review that says C-peptide, insulin and proinsulin cannot reliably separate type 1 from type 2 diabetes except at the extremes, and that islet autoantibodies are the test that establishes autoimmune type 1 diabetes. It mentions a C-peptide <0.6 ng/mL threshold only as 'suggested' by another source and cites overlap studies. It also describes type B insulin resistance (insulin receptor antibodies) and insulin autoimmune syndrome as rare causes.
papers.quote: Only at the extremes of very high or very low levels of insulin secretion can metabolic testing differentiate T1D and T2D.
papers.key_numbers: C-peptide <0.6 ng/mL 'suggested' to identify insulin deficiency (secondary citation); IAA not to be sought after 14 or more days of insulin treatment; islet autoantibody frequencies at T1D onset (ICA 70 to 80%, IAA 50% in children, IA-2A and ZnT8A about 60%).
papers.role_in_work: Background support for the limit of C-peptide in diabetes classification (row 6) and for assay notes; not a source for a score.
papers.design: Narrative review with a table of guideline-type statements on islet autoantibody testing.
papers.population_and_size: Not a study; adults and children with new diabetes.
papers.measure_type: C-peptide (random or fasting, discussed qualitatively) and non-insulin surrogate (islet autoantibodies); no stimulated C-peptide data.
papers.assay_or_platform: Autoantibody assays (RBA, ELISA, ECL, LIPS); notes that proficiency testing for islet autoantibodies cannot be purchased. No C-peptide assay detail.
papers.quality_note: Review by laboratory authors, no systematic search; no conflicts declared in the text read. Not a guideline in itself.

papers.relied_on: Row 27 D4 used it as showing that monitoring practices around pancreas and islet transplant are not standardized.
papers.full_text_shows: It is a survey of 24 pancreas and 18 islet allotransplant programs, not of TPIAT (autotransplant), and it is about which tests programs use, not assay standardization. Fasting C-peptide is routine (92% of pancreas, 94% of islet programs); MMTT is recommended annually after year one by 72% of islet programs (13/18) and in 'for cause' work-up by 83%; no objective cutoffs were endorsed. The 'absence of standardized strategies' is cited from a 2015 meeting, not found by the survey.
papers.quote: Thus, no strict objective cutoffs were endorsed for any of the assays or "for cause" evaluation.
papers.key_numbers: 100% of 42 invited programs responded; pancreas programs: fasting C-peptide routine 92%, random C-peptide 25% and fasting insulin 29% (not recommended); islet programs: fasting C-peptide 94.4%, MMTT annually 72.2% (13/18), MMTT for cause 83.3% (15/18); consensus tiers 45 to 60% suggested, 60 to 75% recommended, >75% strongly recommended.
papers.role_in_work: Practice evidence for the post-transplant graft-function part of row 27 and row 10; weak support for the D4 'unstandardized' wording.
papers.design: International expert-program survey with pre-set agreement thresholds (REDCap), 2019 to 2021.
papers.population_and_size: 24 pancreas and 18 islet transplant programs (North America 18, Europe 18 of 42), selected experienced centres.
papers.measure_type: C-peptide, fasting and random (static), and stimulated (MMTT) in islet programs; fasting insulin also asked.
papers.assay_or_platform: Not reported (no assay or platform information).
papers.quality_note: Opinion survey of selected centres, selection bias acknowledged; not a guideline; allograft recipients, not TPIAT.

papers.relied_on: Row 49 D7 used TrialNet screening of more than 250,000 relatives with about 2.5% multiple-autoantibody positive.
papers.full_text_shows: The table gives '>250,000' relatives screened and '>=2 AA+: 2.5%' (AA+ 5%); the running text says 'over 220,000', a small internal inconsistency. The paper is about autoantibody screening and staging by OGTT or HbA1c; it names no insulin or C-peptide test in staging or follow-up and says 'standards for metabolic follow-up have not been established'.
papers.quote: Standards for metabolic follow-up have not been established but may involve HbA1c levels, random glucose levels, OGTTs, or continuous glucose monitoring.
papers.key_numbers: TrialNet >250,000 relatives (text: over 220,000), AA+ 5%, >=2 AA+ 2.5%; about 90% of new type 1 diabetes has no family history; Fr1da 0.31% of 90,632 children >=2 AA+; DKA at diagnosis 25 to 62% falls to 4 to 6% with monitoring.
papers.role_in_work: Source of the screening denominator in D7 of row 49 (stage 1 and 2 type 1 diabetes monitoring).
papers.design: Narrative status report and perspective with a table of screening programs.
papers.population_and_size: Programs, not a cohort; relatives aged 3 to 45 in TrialNet; general-population programs in US and Europe.
papers.measure_type: non-insulin surrogate (islet autoantibodies, genetic risk score); glucose-based staging (OGTT, HbA1c); no insulin or C-peptide measure.
papers.assay_or_platform: Radiobinding assays, ELISA, ECL, LIPS, ADAP for autoantibodies; no insulin or C-peptide assay.
papers.quality_note: Perspective by programme investigators; several authors report industry consulting in the text (disclosures read in part). Counts are cumulative and from 2021 to 2022 programme reports.

proposals.reason: Within the stated population the only quantitative comparisons now readable show fasting insulin and HOMA-IR performing worse than fasting glucose and OGTT (C238, adults on antipsychotics: AUC 0.72 and 0.80 vs 0.935 and 0.947), and the only child study (C258) is circular, so it cannot show added value. Anchor 0 is 'alternatives do as well or better'. Caveats: C238 is adult, one centre, and its reference includes the glucose tests; no study tested incremental value, so the claim is 'no added value shown', which is why confidence is low. Keeping 1 is defensible if the user reads clarification 19 as scoring mechanism only.
proposals.quote: caseness being defined by HOMA-IR percentile

proposals.reason: Score rests on CAMESA grade-3 expert opinion (case series or expert opinion), which the full texts do not change. C258 removes the 'accuracy-type' study from the evidence (circular reference), and C238 supplies adult accuracy data showing weak performance, but neither tests a decision, so 1 stays.
proposals.quote: caseness being defined by HOMA-IR percentile

proposals.reason: C240 confirms 830 TPIAT in 12 years (about 70 a year, rising; weighted national estimates, adults) and 155 in 2012 from the companion source; the point estimate of about 250 a year remains an unsourced extrapolation but stays in bin 1 (100 to 1,000).
proposals.quote: is a low volume procedure performed in centers scattered throughout the United States and the world

proposals.reason: C244 confirms 5.75 (5.08 to 6.42) per 1,000 person-years for sulfonylurea without insulin. The decisive share (5 to 20% of events worked up with insulin, C-peptide and drug screen) and the 5 to 10 million user count are still assumptions and the paper is silent on them; the rate is a lower bound for all events.
proposals.quote: 6.7-fold higher (IRR, 6.73 [95% CI, 4.93-9.22]) among patients treated with sulfonylurea (without insulin)

proposals.reason: C262 says nothing about assay standardization and does not cover TPIAT; it does not move D4 either way. The score stands on the other cited sources (C-peptide assay literature); under clarification 25 the timed MMTT is a D5 matter.
proposals.quote: Thus, no strict objective cutoffs were endorsed for any of the assays or "for cause" evaluation.

proposals.reason: C263 confirms the TrialNet denominator (>250,000 relatives, 2.5% with two or more autoantibodies; text says over 220,000). The number of people identified and followed per year remains an assumption and the bin (2 or 3, low confidence) is unchanged.

claim_issues.where: usecases/scoring/V26.json row 50 D2 reason (and D8 reason)
claim_issues.issue: Describes C258 as 'one small accuracy-type study (n = 55, HOMA-IR cut point 1.98, reference standard not stated in the abstract)'. The full text states the reference: caseness was defined by the HOMA-IR percentile (>=75th), so the sensitivity and specificity of 83% are circular and are not accuracy for dysglycaemia.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: One small uncontrolled paediatric monitoring study (n = 55) in which the HOMA-IR cut point of 1.98 was derived against a label defined by HOMA-IR percentile itself (circular; not diagnostic accuracy).

claim_issues.issue: Calls C238 an 'adult SGA inpatient study'. The full text describes 798 consecutively admitted adult psychiatric patients on antipsychotics of both generations (first-generation drugs among them), in one Belgian centre, and says insulin and HOMA-IR were tested and were less accurate than the glucose tests; the reason says only that insulin was not used.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: An adult single-centre study of 798 patients on antipsychotics (first and second generation) tested fasting insulin and HOMA-IR against glucose-based diabetes definitions: AUC 0.72 and 0.80 against 0.935 for fasting glucose and 0.947 for 2-h OGTT; its recommended algorithm used HbA1c then fasting glucose and OGTT. Incremental value of insulin was not tested.

claim_issues.issue: 'A 2022 survey of transplant programs reports that monitoring practices are not standardized' is not a finding of the survey: that wording is background cited from a 2015 meeting; the survey covers pancreas and islet allotransplant programs (not TPIAT) and has no assay or standardization data.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: A 2022 survey of 24 pancreas and 18 islet allotransplant programs found fasting C-peptide in routine use (92% and 94%) and MMTT recommended annually by 72% of islet programs, with no objective cutoffs endorsed; it does not address assay standardization or TPIAT.

claim_issues.issue: '830 TPIAT in 2002 to 2013' is a 12-year total of weighted national estimates in adults without neoplasia (about 70 a year on average); the reason does not say it excludes children and that the last year in the data is 2013.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: 830 adult TPIAT for pancreatitis over 2002 to 2013 (weighted national estimate from a 20% discharge sample; neoplasia and under-18 excluded), about 70 a year on average; later volume not found.

notes: Read only local files; no web access used. Tool calls used: about 22 of 40. No score entry in V26, V20, V1 or V22 for these rows carries an original_score or correction key; the only supersedes found is V7 over U1:D7, which is not relevant here. Rows 3, 27, 49 and 50 were not checked in later correction files beyond that. Path to viability: row 50 is not changed by these papers (it still needs a study of insulin's incremental value over fasting glucose, HbA1c and OGTT in treated youth, with an independent reference); row 49 and row 3 are not affected. C258 was extracted from a PDF with interleaved columns; the key sentences were still readable, but quotes may cross column breaks. C238 and C240 text is from XML and is clean. C261 and C263 are not cited by any score entry that reads their content (C261 only appears in V16 assumptions as fetched at abstract level), so for them 'proposals' are null by design; claims.csv, usecases-verified.md and merged-conclusion.md contain none of the six PMIDs, so no claim in those documents needed checking against them. Assumption: C262's 'for cause' MMTT figure of 83.3% comes from the islet-program paragraph (15/18) and the pancreas-program percentages from the earlier paragraphs.
